title: Emotional Leakage
description: How strong hidden emotions unintentionally 'leak' out through peripheral body channels.

sections.title: Quick Understanding
sections.content: Despite our best efforts to control our faces and words, strong hidden emotions often leak out through other channels of the body. When the brain is focused on lying or masking, it often forgets to control the feet, hands, and voice.

sections.title: What It Looks Like
content: A perfectly calm face, but feet that are bouncing rapidly.
Sounding totally confident, but clenching the hands tightly under the desk.
Smiling warmly, while a single drop of sweat forms on the forehead.

sections.title: What It May Indicate
content: An emotion fighting entirely against the person's conscious control.
A discrepancy between public performance and private feeling.

sections.title: What It Does NOT Mean
content: Leakage does NOT tell you exactly what the person is thinking, only what they are feeling.
Leakage is NOT always negative. You can leak extreme excitement while trying to act professionally calm.

sections.title: Real Life Examples
content: Poker: A player holds a perfectly stoic 'poker face', but the carotid artery on their neck is visibly pounding quickly because they have a great hand.
Workplace: A manager calmly reads a difficult company announcement, but their hands holding the paper are visibly trembling.
Dating: Someone acting totally cool and disinterested, but their foot is pointed directly at their crush and tapping nervously.

sections.title: Cluster Analysis
content: Calm face + heavy breathing + gripping the chair = Suppressed panic or rage.
Bored tone of voice + pupil dilation + leaning forward = Suppressed intense interest.

sections.title: Common Situations
content: Concealing a surprise or a secret.

sections.title: Observation Mistakes
sections.content: Mistake: Focusing solely on the person's face. Reality: People are heavily trained to control their facial expressions. They are rarely trained to control their feet.

sections.title: Practical Observation Tips
content: Start your observation from the ground up. The feet and legs are the most honest parts of the body because we rarely think about controlling them.
Watch the hands. If the hands are hidden in pockets or under a table, they may be leaking stress (wringing, picking at nails) that the person doesn't want you to see.

sections.title: Red Flags
content: Extreme rigidity. Sometimes the leakage isn't motion, but the complete, unnatural absence of motion as the person uses all their energy to hold themselves together.

sections.title: Reality Check
sections.content: Emotional leakage is a valuable clue that the internal emotional state does not match the external performance. Use it to dig deeper into the conversation, not as an instant final proof of deception.
